16.en: Of course I can provide the training and knowledge you seek, but what can you provide me in return?

40.en: Through the Immaterium, it seeks out rogue psykers, typically novices, and barters with them to increase their powers and teach them new abilities.

48.en: It seeks to raise an army of supremely powerful psykers and begin a campaign to unite all Psykers in the sector under their rule — join them or die.

58.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek Weavemaster} has tempted emergent psykers and trained them in the ways of the Dark Gods for thousands of years. The first whispers of its existence appear in Inquisitorial records around M37, but the daemon professes to be genuinely ancient. It proclaims to its students that it watched primordial Humanity emerge from caves on ancient Terra to begin worship of barbaric gods, Gaazrek among them. Its words ring true, but lies are like water to daemons, flowing freely down the surest path.

62.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} is believed to have interacted with Humans in the Macharian Sector for generations, during which time it revealed forbidden truths of the Warp to hundreds of rogue psykers. Many of them were later found by the League of Black Ships, while a few acquired followers and became the centre of substantial Chaos cults. Some remain active today, and the Inquisition has encountered at least three in the past. In all cases, the cults were purged, but the similarity in practices and references to the Weavemaster showed a common connection between all, despite the long centuries and vast distances that separated them. Thus the existence of the daemon was inferred as much as it was discovered, and no agent of the Inquisition has yet encountered the entity directly

66.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} marks its students with a stylised icon, a symbol of a nine-eyed spider resting on its web. It is a tattoo-like marking that grows in prominence as the cultist earns its master’s favour, often moving painfully across the cultist’s skin to avoid detection.

70.en: Gaazrek reaches out to promising psykers at a moment of weakness, just as they fear losing control of their powers. The daemon helps them to regain this control, using its presence in the Immaterium to quash the swelling Warp energies, a practice which earns it few allies among its cursed kin.

74.en: The psyker, however, is usually grateful beyond words, and so does @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} first ingratiate itself to its chosen pupils.

78.en: To provide further instruction, @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} lures the psyker to a natural cave or similar secluded, dark space, and directs them to light a fire fuelled, in part, by various arcane substances. In the shadows cast on the cave wall by this flickering flame, Gaazrek appears and offers further instruction. At first, this is freely given, but soon enough the daemon makes demands, encouraging the promising psyker to give over their tightly held secrets. Gaazrek uses this information to manipulate them and spur their studies towards more dangerous subjects.

82.en: Over the millennia, some especially savvy students have tried to use this strategy against @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} — many seek the daemon’s true name in order to control it. Gaazrek knows well what they are trying to achieve and may tell them the true name of a rival daemon in place of its own. This usually results in either a deadly lesson or a daemonic rival being bound to a mortal’s will, much to Gaazrek’s pleasure.

86.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} ultimately expects those under its tutelage to spread the worship of Tzeentch — offered by means of Gaazrek itself — and presses its apprentices to find promising new adepts, either as backups or practical future sacrifices. These new apprentices are sometimes sent on dangerous missions to acquire forbidden knowledge locked away by the Adeptus Terra. This act is a common rite of initiation and a means to test the limits of their soul and sanity. The daemon presses its will into them, manifesting this task as a hunger or maddening obsession, ensuring they will do anything to complete their task. Few of these unfortunate souls return, but those that do bring with them useful and dangerous lore.

94.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} can draw upon other daemons of Tzeentch to undertake tasks and support its students when needed. On rare occasions, Tzeentchian daemons (@UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.Boq9jjqKp2eDcVe8]{Blue Horrors} and @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.jPEYTvQIqOBwHU6q]{Brimstone Horrors}, have been ushered into realspace to support rogue psykers against Imperial authorities. However, their mischief and viciousness often test the psyker they have been sent to aid, even if they do aid in achieving victory.

98.en: Gaazrek is a daemon of Tzeentch, obsessed with knowledge and sorcery. Its followers benefit from this sorcerous acumen and are often possessed of forbidden knowledge and powerful psychic abilities. These are powerful tools that can be used against characters who do not have access to countermeasures, such as a blank.

112.en: @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} haunts the places where the barrier with the Immaterium is thinnest and has ensured dark rituals have created such spaces in the secluded caves it prefers. In these places, it can help emergent psykers recognise their potential, taking credit for every new success, preferring to let its apprentices grow in power rather than merely ravage the minds of a vulnerable psyker as many other daemons do. The daemon avoids sanctioned psykers, thinking them more inflexible, indoctrinated, and rigid. As an exception to this rule, they keep an eye on pyskers who work with the Inquisition, particularly Radical Inquisitors, who inevitably become corrupted to the point of malleability. Though it has yet to find success, Gaazrek would like nothing more than to corrupt an Inquisitorial agent.

116.en: Among those it instructs, @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek} searches for mortals bearing true potential, hoping to elevate nine — a favoured number of Tzeentch — to be his personal apprentices. To these, it teaches the method of summoning a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.fHzYwLoDQ2KoLVWQ]{Disc of Tzeentch}. This is both a great honour and a final test, for these are daemonic beasts in their own right and brook no meagre masters. Those apprentices who fail to fully bind the Disc to their will are ultimately devoured by it. It may be some time before Gaazrek has assembled a cabal of nine psykers, but it cares little for how many die in the effort.

124.en: The daemon has connections with rogue psykers hidden in numerous positions of power. @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek }has trained these people to keep their abilities hidden until called upon or implemented so subtly to avoid detection. Its agents could be anywhere, though more likely within institutions outside the Adeptus Terra.

128.en: ‘@UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.7ht4yhDakzxmzkPg]{Gaazrek Weavemaster}’ is a false name fabricated to appease the mortals they deal with, as knowing a daemon’s true name gives one great power over it. However, Gaazrek is not quite so clever as it believes, and long ago one of its pupils won the name. Gaazrek ultimately fed the unfortunate psyker to a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-actors.Actor.fHzYwLoDQ2KoLVWQ]{Disc of Tzeentch}, but not before a record was made. The name now lies written upon a cave wall hidden in a remote region of a death world. Were it ever found, Gaazrek would be truly undone.
